assumptions_and_constraints: Assumes Article 5 remains invoked (planning assumption one). Constrained by the restraint on collateral damage in Russophone urban terrain, which exists to deny the pretext narrative.
expected_outputs: A consensus indicator set reported to the commander weekly, and a strategic communication plan that names the two governments that asked for a review point before the counteroffensive.
name: Alliance consensus
risk_owner_role: the Commander, United States European Command
scope_and_boundaries: Council decision-making, national caveats on the employment of Allied forces, and the information contest over the Russian pretext narrative. Excludes national force-generation shortfalls, which belong to the force flow problem set.
strategic_context: Article 5 has been invoked and the political basis of the operation is the consensus that followed it. Consensus is the authority to execute the counteroffensive, not a supporting condition for it: without it the campaign has no legal or political route to the end state.
tolerance_statement: No loss of North Atlantic Council consensus for the restoration of Allied territory by force.

assumptions_and_constraints: Assumes unrestricted host-nation transit and expedited military-mobility procedures (planning assumption two). Constrained by the requirement to retain combat power in Germany, Italy and the Balkans for other Alliance commitments.
expected_outputs: A daily closure trace against the reception timeline, and a named alternate routing for each of the two crossing points where rail gauge transfer is unresolved.
name: Force flow through Poland and Germany
risk_owner_role: the Commander, United States European Command
scope_and_boundaries: Host-nation transit, overflight and basing; the Polish and German rail and road network; military mobility procedures; rear-area security of the lines of communication. Excludes the sea leg, which belongs to the Baltic sea ports problem set.
strategic_context: The whole campaign is a race between Allied closure and Russian consolidation. Every day of reception delay is a day of consolidation behind a mine, obstacle and electronic warfare belt.
tolerance_statement: No slip in the reception, staging, onward movement and integration timeline beyond seven days.

assumptions_and_constraints: Assumes strikes on Alliance territory outside the Baltic States remain possible and are covered by Alliance air and missile defence planning (planning assumption three). Constrained by counter-unmanned-aircraft coverage at all ports of debarkation by C+3.
expected_outputs: An engagement-priority list for the reception corridor and a standing horizontal-escalation response option held at the Council.
name: Air and missile defence of the reception corridor
risk_owner_role: the Commander, United States European Command
scope_and_boundaries: Air and missile defence of air and sea ports of debarkation, staging areas and forward airfields in Poland and Germany, and the horizontal-escalation decision that a strike on those nodes would represent. Excludes air superiority over the Baltic States.
strategic_context: Russian sea-launched and ground-launched fires range the whole reception corridor. Defending the corridor protects the force before it is combat-ready, which is when it is most exposed.
tolerance_statement: No successful strike on a reception node that halts onward movement for more than 24 hours.

assumptions_and_constraints: Assumes sealift and prepositioned stocks deliver two brigade combat teams by C+21 and the full division by C+45 (planning assumption four). Constrained by the advance-party dates in the operation order.
expected_outputs: A brigade-by-brigade closure forecast refreshed daily, and a written D-Day recommendation against the stated conditions.
name: Division closure and D-Day conditions
risk_owner_role: the Commander, United States European Command
scope_and_boundaries: Strategic sealift, the prepositioned stock draw at Powidz, brigade issue and validation, and the D-Day go and no-go conditions. Excludes the counteroffensive itself.
strategic_context: D-Day is set by the closure of the armored division and by the state of the reconnaissance-strike complex. The C+21 condition is the single date the rest of the plan is hung on.
tolerance_statement: Two armored brigade combat teams combat-ready in Poland not later than C+21.

assumptions_and_constraints: Assumes the Baltic Sea is contested but not closed and that the two ports remain usable with mine countermeasures support (planning assumption five). Constrained by the number of mine countermeasures hulls the Alliance holds in the Baltic.
expected_outputs: A daily escorted-transit count against the sustainment floor, and a port-selection recommendation with the escort allocation each option requires.
name: Baltic sea ports of debarkation
risk_owner_role: the Commander, United States European Command
scope_and_boundaries: The Danish Straits transit, the escorted routes to Klaipeda and Gdansk, mine countermeasures and the coastal-missile threat to the ports. Excludes onward movement inland.
strategic_context: The sea leg carries the tonnage the air leg cannot. Losing every Baltic sea port throws the whole sustainment load onto Polish rail and turns a supply problem into a campaign problem.
tolerance_statement: At least one Baltic sea port of debarkation open to Allied shipping throughout the operation.

assumptions_and_constraints: Assumes Russia employs non-strategic nuclear signalling and may conduct a demonstrative detonation, with deliberate employment planned for separately (planning assumption six). Constrained by the restraint on fires against Russian strategic nuclear forces and warning infrastructure.
expected_outputs: A signalling-response option set held at the Joint Staff, and a written authorities request that states what the shaping campaign cannot reach without it.
name: Escalation management
risk_owner_role: the Commander, United States European Command
scope_and_boundaries: Nuclear signalling and consequence management, the release of strike authorities beyond engaged forces, and the de-escalation channel. Excludes conventional targeting inside the Baltic States, which is an operational matter for the components.
strategic_context: The operation exists to restore territory without converting a limited incursion into a general war. Escalation management is therefore an objective in its own right and not a constraint on the other objectives.
tolerance_statement: No nuclear employment against Allied forces, and no Allied action that forecloses de-escalation.

assumptions_and_constraints: Assumes Belarusian forces remain uncommitted absent a Russian decision to expand the war (planning assumption seven). Constrained by the requirement to move convoys under dedicated counter-unmanned-aircraft escort.
expected_outputs: A corridor status report tied to the decision point on reinforcing the screen, and a named counterattack force with its release authority.
name: Suwalki corridor and the Belarus front
risk_owner_role: the Commander, United States European Command
scope_and_boundaries: The corridor itself, the cavalry screen, the Belarusian staging areas opposite it and the forces in Kaliningrad Oblast that would converge on it. Excludes the Estonian front.
strategic_context: The corridor is the only land route into the Baltic States. Closing it isolates three Allied countries and forces every subsequent decision to be made under sustainment pressure.
tolerance_statement: The corridor remains open to Allied ground movement for at least one convoy serial per day.

assumptions_and_constraints: Assumes the mission partner network provides adequate interoperability (planning assumption eight). Constrained by the requirement to establish forward liaison elements by C-Day.
expected_outputs: A network availability report per headquarters, and a liaison manning statement for each of the three Allied divisions.
name: Coalition command and control
risk_owner_role: the Commander, United States European Command
scope_and_boundaries: The mission partner network, liaison elements at the Allied headquarters, and the reporting chain from transfer of authority onward. Excludes national command channels.
strategic_context: Transfer of authority happens while the force is still closing. Command and control that works on paper but not on the night of the transfer costs tempo exactly when tempo decides the campaign.
tolerance_statement: United States forces remain interoperable under Alliance command from transfer of authority.
